newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to see first interactive ads this month.
newsitem.headline: Germany to see first interactive ads this month.

text.p: German digital television channel DF1 said on Wednesday it plans to introduce interactive advertising to viewers by the end of the month.

The new technology will allow viewers to switch between various ads for a single product with the press of a button on a digital decoder box, sales director Nils Roehrig told Reuters at the two-day German TV ad fair.
Viewers should have access to interactive ads by August 25, when the channel will broadcast from the U.S. Open tennis tournament, Roehrig said.

Further expansion of interactive possibilities for ads are planned for later this year, which will allow viewers to request further information about advertised products and services with messages sent over telephone lines.

DF1 also plans to make the most popular company home pages available on digital television sets by the first half of 1998, which Roehrig said will provide faster access to the sites than a personal computer.
Roehrig is sales director for sports channel DSF and DF1, both of which belong to the Munich-based Kirch Group.
